encodings.name: Door block _1D<q><L|R><cm> with nested LEAF + SWING
layers: DOOR (the _1D insert and its nested LEAF/SWING inserts; their geometry is on layer 0 and inherits DOOR)
encodings.entities: INSERT _1D3R90 or _1D0L100 at scale +-1000 (block unit = metre). Inside: INSERT SWING (one ARC) and INSERT LEAF (closed LWPOLYLINE 0.035 x 1.0), both at the block origin, plus 2 ATTDEFs.
encodings.meaning: '_1D' = one-leaf hinged door. The digit = quarter turns applied to LEAF/SWING inside the block (0 = 0 deg, 3 = 270 deg). L/R = hand (R = LEAF/SWING mirrored inside the block, sx<0). The number = leaf width in cm, which equals the clear width between the jambs (90 -> 0.90 m, 100 -> 1.00 m). In the base door (0, L) the opening runs along local +x from the hinge, the leaf is drawn open along +y, and the arc runs from the closed tip (1,0) to the leaf's outer corner (0.035,1). The INSERT's own rotation and mirroring apply on top (C3C4 is inserted with sy=-1000). LEAF world y-scale = leaf length (900 or 1000 mm); x-scale 1000 = 35 mm thickness. The insert point is the hinge. It lies on the wall face on the swing side, exactly at the inner face of the hinge-side JAMB.
encodings.howToGetEnds: Hinge H = the insert point (world coordinates). Closed tip C = the SWING arc end that is not at the leaf's free end (exact). H..C is the clear opening. Add the 50 mm JAMB at each end to reach the jamb outer faces, which equal the wall ends to +-1 mm; that is the structural opening. Centre line = H moved half the wall thickness away from the swing side: 0.05 m in 0.10 m walls, 0.125 m in the 0.25 m wall of G-D07, where the 0.10 m jambs sit flush with the swing face. Do not take the arc centre as the hinge: SWING has r = 0.983 x width and is centred (0.018, 0.018) x scale from the hinge, about 23 mm off.
encodings.counts: Ground 5: 3 x _1D3R90 (G-D04, G-D06, G-D07) and 2 x _1D0L100 (G-D02, G-D03). Upper 1: _1D3R90 (U-D04). Each has 1 nested LEAF and 1 nested SWING. No duplicates. 12 DSYM attributes, all empty.
encodings.edgeCases: The name grammar belongs to this office; for other offices read the geometry inside the block. G-D02 sits in a 0.10 m wall whose face lines run straight through, so there is no wall gap and the merged wall closes it. G-D06 has the face of a perpendicular wall on one side, so the wall end has no collinear partner. G-D07 is in a 0.25 m wall drawn with 4 lines, and a room-outline polyline runs along its face. Some inserts are mirrored (sy<0).

encodings.name: Loose LEAF insert (no door block) with a separate swing arc
layers: WIN (the arcs of the upper toilet doors)
WALL (the arc of G-D08, inside block hjkhkk)
encodings.entities: INSERT LEAF at sx=1000 (35 mm thick) and sy=+-550 (a 0.55 m leaf; one has sy=-1000, a 1.0 m leaf), drawn open at 90 deg. A separate 3-point ARC runs from the closed tip to the leaf tip. It is not centred on the hinge (fitted r 0.62-0.64 for a 0.60 m clear opening). Usually a JAMB pair as well.
encodings.meaning: A hinged door leaf. |sy| = leaf length in mm; the sign of sy together with the rotation gives the side the leaf lies on. The leaf is 50 mm shorter than the clear opening (0.55 against 0.60); the JAMB pair defines the opening.
encodings.howToGetEnds: Hinge = insert point (on the inner face of the hinge JAMB). Closed tip = the arc end away from the leaf tip (0.60 m from the hinge). Structural ends = the JAMB outer faces = the wall ends (0.70 m).
encodings.counts: Ground: 7 inserts, 5 unique. 4 are top level (G-D11, G-D12, G-D13, G-D14); G-D08's leaf (E13E) is repeated twice inside block hjkhkk. Upper: 2 (U-D16, U-D17, inside the xref block). Neither floor has a loose SWING insert: all 6 SWINGs are inside _1D blocks.
encodings.edgeCases: The leaf length is not the opening width. G-D08's leaf (E13E and its hjkhkk copies) has extrusion (0,0,-1). Its dxf.insert is therefore in OCS, and prims.py stores (-36.748, 20.808) while the geometry is at +36.748; use the full WCS matrix. That door's swing arc is on WALL, so the pipeline treats it as a wall line. G-D14 has only one JAMB.

encodings.name: Swing arcs on any layer, with a leaf (including pivot doors)
layers: false hits: WALL-GL (shower doors), XR_L44$0$I-FURN and XR_L44$0$Layer7 (chairs, fridge), TREE
encodings.entities: ARC, usually a quarter circle (sweep 85-95 deg). 3-point arcs sweep 71-79 deg; one half-open xref leaf sweeps 52 deg. The leaf is a thin rectangle (20-39 mm), a pair of lines, or a single line.
encodings.meaning: A door swing. One arc end is the leaf tip (open position); the other is the closed position on the wall line. Pivot doors (G-D05 at 1.75 m, G-D10 at 1.20 m) have a leaf drawn across the opening, a pivot 0.2-0.75 m in from one end, and two arcs, all on layer 0.
encodings.howToGetEnds: Use the arc END POINTS. The closed tip and the hinge (the leaf's far end) bound the clear opening. Snap both outward to the nearest jamb outer face, wall end or perpendicular wall face within 0.15 m. For pivot doors, the ends are the two wall or pier faces the arcs end on.
encodings.counts: Real door swings. Ground: 15 doors, 17 unique arcs = 5 SWING in _1D blocks, 1 loose DOOR arc (the site gate), 9 unique layer-0 arcs for 7 doors including the 2 pivot doors, 1 WALL arc, 1 A-DOOR arc. Upper: 14 doors, 21 arcs = 1 SWING, 4 I-DOOR, 1 A-DOOR, 14 WIN. False arcs: 1 WALL-GL shower door per floor, chairs and a fridge in the furniture xref, 2 TREE quarter circles of r=1.0 (no wall gap behind them).
encodings.edgeCases: 29 of the 32 doors have an arc; the 3 pocket sliding doors do not. 3-point arcs are not centred on the hinge. D4's arc is CENTER2 and A$C83adbef5's is HIDDEN2, so a continuous-lines-only filter would drop them. U-D01 has a half-open leaf (52 deg). Arcs are duplicated (hjkhkk is inserted twice; layer-0 copies). The leaf finder must prefer thin rectangles: a naive one matched TREE lines as leaves at U-D16/U-D17.

encodings.name: JAMB block pairs (D-JAMB)
encodings.entities: INSERT JAMB = a unit-square LWPOLYLINE scaled (+-50, +-100) or (+-100, +-50), giving a rectangle 50 mm along the wall by 100 mm across it. The insert point is one corner of that rectangle.
encodings.meaning: The door frame or jamb on each side of a door (also around two fixed glass panels). The 100 mm side spans the whole of a 0.10 m wall, or sits flush with the swing face of a thicker wall.
encodings.howToGetEnds: Pair two rectangles whose 100 mm sides cover the same interval across the wall (+-15 mm) and that face each other 0.3-2.6 m apart. Structural opening = outer face to outer face; clear opening = inner faces = leaf width. Wall face lines end flush with the jamb outer faces to +-1 mm.
encodings.counts: Ground: 24 inserts, 22 unique, giving 10 pairs (G-D01, D02, D03, D04, D06, D07, D11, D12, D13, W14) and 2 single jambs. Upper: 30 inserts, 14-15 unique (each is repeated inside the xref block), giving 6 pairs (U-D04, D09, D15, D16, D17, W12) and single jambs at U-D13 and U-D14.
encodings.edgeCases: All 16 pairs are real openings, but they find only 14 of the 32 doors. Inserts are duplicated. Some doors have a single jamb. Around fixed glass (G-W14, U-W12) the wall lines run on between the jambs. Window end pieces on D-JAMB have the same 50 x 100 size, so pair by facing distance and by what lies between (arc or leaf -> door; glass line -> window).

encodings.name: Loose D-JAMB pieces: 50x100 end pieces, 50x50 sash stiles, cladding outlines, finish lines
encodings.entities: LWPOLYLINE rectangles of 50x100 mm and 50x50 mm (often open 5-point polylines), larger outlines, and LINEs. Many are inside blocks hjkhkk, jkljlll and the upper xref.
encodings.meaning: Frame pieces of windows and sliding units: a 100x50 piece flush against each wall end, one 50x50 stile per sliding track, and two 50x50 squares side by side where the sashes meet. The outlines are cladding around the entrance piers and some walls; the finished face is 50 mm proud of the wall line. Long LINEs are finish lines along wall faces (for example x 36.678 / 36.698).
encodings.howToGetEnds: Take the outermost 100x50 piece at each end of a window band: its outer face is the opening end, flush with the wall or column face to +-1 mm. At clad piers the glazing stops at the cladding face, 50 mm short of the wall line (9 window ends).
encodings.counts: Unique pieces. Ground: 50 of 50x100, 76 of 50x50, 8 outlines, 56 lines. Upper: 41, 56, 0, 56. Raw counts are 2-3 times higher because of duplicates.
encodings.edgeCases: The same layer carries cladding and finish lines. Two sliding units consist only of D-JAMB pieces and slide arrows, with no glass lines (G-W17, G-W20). Duplicates throughout.

encodings.entities: 3 closed LWPOLYLINE rectangles, 39 mm x 1.58 / 3.08 / 1.58 m. Each lies parallel to a wall and partly inside a wall pocket: a 50-80 mm slot between wall lines, with no closing line across the slot.

encodings.name: Window bands on WIN (2-6 parallel lines, 25 or 50 mm apart, 50-125 mm deep)
layers: sometimes a WALL-GL glass line or A_Grill
encodings.entities: LINEs and a few LWPOLYLINEs. Ground windows are mostly inside block hjkhkk (inserted twice at the same point on layer WALL) or block jkljlll; upper windows are inside the xref block.
encodings.meaning: Glazing. Patterns: 5 lines at 25 mm = a 100 mm frame with 2 sliding tracks (most windows); 3 lines at 50 mm = fixed or single-track; 4 lines (mixed 25/50); 3 lines at 25 mm = 50 mm frames in 1.0 m units (block jkljlll, partition G-W13). There are no sill lines anywhere, so the plan cannot tell a window from floor-length glass. The 8 tags AW1/AW12/AW14/AW17/D1/D3/AD1 appear only on the right-hand elevation.

wallEndsAtOpenings:
Measured on all 92 reviewed openings (184 ends), using the pipeline's own wall lines (house3d.json).

(1) The wall stops at 123 ends: both face lines end within 12 mm of the opening end. At 108 of these 123 (88%) there is also a closing LINE across the wall thickness on the wall layer: 37 of 46 door ends, 34 of 36 passage ends, 37 of 41 window ends. The 15 without a closing line are T-junctions where the wall turns, the pocket mouths of the sliding doors (U-D06 to U-D08, with a slot left open), or stubs.

(2) 12 ends are the face of a perpendicular wall or column. These are openings at L-junctions (G-D06, G-D11 against a column, U-P01) and window bays. A further 27 ends are a glazing end, a clad pier, a column box or a free corner.

(3) Jambs never hide wall ends. At 86 of the 95 jamb ends where a wall line ends, the wall face line ends exactly at the jamb's outer face (+-1 mm, once +4 mm). The other 9 are clad piers, where the glazing stops at the D-JAMB cladding face 50 mm proud of the structural wall line. JAMB blocks sit inside the opening; _1D and LEAF insert points are on the jambs' inner faces.

(4) 12 openings are bridged: wall-layer lines run through at least 90% of the span.
- 8 by the wall's own face lines. Doors: G-D02 (_1D0L100), G-D09 (xref D4) and U-D05 (WIN door), where the lines are continuous through the door. Glass panels: G-W09, G-W14, U-W02 (only the inner 0.10 m of a 0.25 m wall), U-W10 and U-W12, where the face lines are split at the jambs and redrawn between them as frame lines.
- 3 by a closed room-outline polyline on WALL (handle E291, tracing the room x 32.398-36.398, y 19.2585-23.109): G-D07 (the wall's own lines stop with closing lines, but the outline runs along the face), G-P06 and G-W17.
- U-D01 sits in a single-line partition (x 83.08) that runs straight through it.

(5) Thickness: most door walls are 0.10 m, the same as the jamb depth. Some walls are 0.25 m, drawn with 3-4 parallel lines (G-D07, G-D10, G-P04/05, G-P07). Door frames sit flush with the swing face, leaving a reveal on the other side.

So wall gaps are trustworthy where they exist (88% have closing lines), but 13% of openings have no gap at all, and about a third of glazed openings sit between columns or perpendicular walls rather than collinear wall ends.
existingMergeAtOpenings:
merge_cad.py closes gaps under 0.24 m. That never touches a real opening here: the narrowest is 0.70 m. What closes openings is line work drawn across them.

Measured on cad_test/src/house3d_merged.json, converted back to drawing metres. Each opening was sampled every 1 cm along 7 lines spread across the wall band; the solids are classed as wall, glass and single.

DOORS, 32 (15 ground, 17 upper):
- 24 open (12 ground, 12 upper).
- 3 closed by a full-height wall solid, because the wall is drawn through: G-D02, G-D09, U-D05.
- 3 filled by a glass strip, because the 3-line WIN threshold bands paired into glass: U-D10, U-D11, U-D12.
- 2 blocked by a 1 m 'single' piece: G-D07 (the room-outline line) and U-D01 (single-line partition).

proposedRules.rule: Normalise before detecting anything. Dedupe identical geometry (1 mm). Transform every nested entity with the full WCS matrix: one LEAF has extrusion (0,0,-1), so its dxf.insert is in OCS. Classify by geometry, never by an INSERT's layer. Keep non-continuous arcs on any layer as possible door evidence. From the wall lines used for gap tests, remove: closed polylines on wall layers that trace a room interior; HIDDEN/dashed boxes; tiny closed shapes. Clip to the building outline (floor plate) so fence and pool lines drop out.
proposedRules.covers: All rules below. Here: duplicates (hjkhkk is inserted twice, so WIN goes from 219 raw lines to 126; JAMB 24 -> 22 on the ground and 30 -> 14 upper), the E291 outline (unblocks G-D07, G-P06, G-W17), the OCS leaf of G-D08, the CENTER2/HIDDEN2 xref door arcs, the W_Grill fence and pool glass.
proposedRules.failureCases: Outline removal could delete a real thin wall drawn as one closed polyline. A dedupe tolerance can merge two genuinely adjacent jamb pieces. A drawing with no reliable outline cannot be clipped.
proposedRules.howToCheck: Compare entity counts before and after per layer. Rerun the merge on Sukhumvit and confirm G-D07, G-P06 and G-W17 become open while the wall-run count stays the same (30 ground, 23 upper). Overlay the result on renders/final_*.png.

proposedRules.rule: Swing door. An ARC on any layer (r 0.3-1.7 m, sweep 40-100 deg) plus a leaf: a thin rectangle 15-60 mm thick, or a line or line pair, running from the hinge to one arc end. Closed tip = the other arc end. Accept only if the hinge-to-tip chord lies on a wall band (wall lines, jambs or glazing within 0.15 m). Snap each end outward to the nearest jamb outer face, wall end, or perpendicular wall or column face within 0.15 m. Two arcs whose closed tips meet = a double door. Several leaves between one pair of end pieces = a door set.
proposedRules.covers: 29 of 32 doors here: 6 _1D blocks, 7 loose LEAFs (layer-0 or WIN arcs), 2 pivot doors, 2 *U31 double doors, 2 A-DOOR xref doors, 10 WIN doors including the two 3-leaf sets, and the site gate. Independent of layer and block name.
proposedRules.failureCases: Pivot doors (G-D05, G-D10): the leaf crosses the opening and there are two arcs, so take the arc end points on the wall line as the ends. Half-open leaf (U-D01, 52 deg). 3-point arcs not centred on the hinge: use end points, never the centre. False arcs: WALL-GL shower doors (chord on a glass line inside a room), furniture arcs (chairs, fridge; no wall band), TREE quarter circles r=1.0 at boundary walls (no gap). Pocket sliding doors have no arc. A naive leaf matcher picked TREE lines at U-D16/U-D17 and a WALL line at U-D05, so prefer thin rectangles and lines on the same layer as the arc.
proposedRules.howToCheck: Run on Sukhumvit against openings.json (32 doors, ends to +-2 cm) and on the presidential suite against the 22 hand-listed DOORS in build_model.py. Report precision and recall and the end error; review contact sheets (renders/op_*.png).

proposedRules.rule: Jamb pair. Two identical small rectangles on any layer (here 50 x 100 mm) whose long sides cover the same interval across the wall (+-15 mm) and face each other 0.3-2.6 m apart. Opening ends = the outer faces; clear width = the inner faces. If an arc or leaf lies between them it is a door; if a glass line does, a window.
proposedRules.covers: 16 of 92 openings (14 doors, 2 glass panels), with 100% precision. Ends correct to +-1 mm, so it is the best snap target for rules 2, 5 and 6, including where the wall is drawn through (G-D02, G-W14, U-W12).
proposedRules.failureCases: Single jambs (G-D14, U-D13, U-D14). Window mullion pieces of the same size: pair only nearest neighbours that have no band line running past them. Offices that draw no jambs. Duplicated jambs.
proposedRules.howToCheck: Match pairs to openings.json and count real vs false (16/16 here). Measure the distance from each jamb outer face to the wall end (86 of 95 flush to +-1 mm).

proposedRules.rule: Collinear wall-end gap. Two wall strips with the same centre line (+-1 cm) and the same thickness (+-1 cm), whose face lines stop facing each other (a closing line across each end is common but not required), with a gap of 0.5-3.0 m. Require no wall-layer geometry inside the gap (lines on glass, window or door layers are allowed) and building on both sides (inside the floor plate). Then classify by what lies inside: arc or leaf -> door; thin parallel band -> glazing; sliding panel -> sliding door; nothing -> passage.
proposedRules.covers: 49 of 92 openings: all 20 passages, 19 of 32 doors and 10 of 40 windows. 50 of the 65 gap locations found were real; 60 if gaps of 0.25 m or less are dropped.
proposedRules.failureCases: Walls drawn straight through the opening (8, plus 3 crossed by a room outline). Openings at L-junctions, where one end is the face of a perpendicular wall or column (G-D06, G-D08, G-D11, U-D07, U-D08, window bays). False gaps: separate buildings sharing a wall line (G017, U104); column-to-wall gaps outside the envelope (G014, G029); stair ends (G057, U105); a column inside the gap (G043); carport posts (G055, G056); a wardrobe carcass on a wall layer (U071).
proposedRules.howToCheck: Score wallgaps.json against openings.json (recall per kind, false gaps by cause). On another office's file, render every gap on a contact sheet (sheet.py) and count.

proposedRules.rule: Glazing band. 1-6 thin lines parallel to the wall (spacing 17-75 mm, total depth 0.13 m or less) on any non-wall layer, spanning within 0.06 m between two bounding elements: wall ends, columns, perpendicular wall faces or jamb pieces. Ends = the outermost jamb piece's outer face, or the bounding face. Reject: 2-line leaves of 20-40 mm that end at an arc (door leaf); bands inside an opening that has an arc (door threshold); small closed shapes (fixtures); lines outside the floor plate (fence, pool); short glass with a glass-door arc inside a room (shower). Kind: a band in a wall gap with wall ends on both sides -> window (default sill); a band spanning a whole bay between columns -> full-height glazing, flagged for staff or read from the elevations.
proposedRules.covers: All 40 glazed openings here, including the HATCH-framed link corridors and the WALL-GL sliding panes, once single lines and offset panels are accepted.
proposedRules.failureCases: Window vs glass wall cannot be decided for bays (about 22 here). Jamb-only units with no glass lines (G-W17, G-W20) need rule 3/4 evidence instead. Bands are triple-counted when blocks are duplicated. Grille lines just outside the wall band (U-W20). Glazed partitions inside the house (G-W13).
proposedRules.howToCheck: Score winbands.json units against openings.json windows (51 real, 21 false here: 9 WIN door leaves, 5 shower screens, pool, fence, 2 fragments of one screen). Compare kinds against the elevation tags where they exist.

proposedRules.rule: Window hidden in a drawn-through wall. A line on a glass or window layer, or the middle line of a 3-line group, runs inside a wall's thickness between two cross pieces (jamb rectangles or short closing lines) while the wall face lines continue across. Cut an opening between the cross pieces; if a swing arc is attached, it is a door.
proposedRules.covers: G-W09, G-W14, U-W02, U-W10, U-W12 and door U-D05: 6 of the 8 openings that the current merge closes with a wall solid. G-D02 and G-D09 are recovered by rules 2 and 3.
proposedRules.failureCases: Long finish or insulation lines inside thick walls on a glass-like layer (none here). Cross pieces missing. Partial bridging (U-W02 bridges only the inner 0.10 m).
proposedRules.howToCheck: After cutting, rerun s13_checks.py: these 6 should change from 'closed by wall solid' to 'glass strip' or 'open'.

proposedRules.rule: Pocket sliding door. A thin rectangle (30-50 mm x 0.6-3.5 m) on any layer, parallel to a wall, with at least 30% of its length inside a slot (two parallel wall lines 40-100 mm apart whose end has no closing line across the slot). The door spans from that pocket mouth to the next wall end, box or corner along the panel's line.
proposedRules.covers: U-D06, U-D07, U-D08; possibly the orphan leaf C367 at G-P07.
proposedRules.failureCases: Shelves and furniture panels. The opening's far end is ambiguous at a free corner (U-D07, U-D08). A half-open panel does not show the full width, so use wall ends.
proposedRules.howToCheck: Visual check on contact sheets; widths against the wall gap (U-D06 = 1.70 m).

proposedRules.rule: Block-name decoding, as a cross-check only. '_1D<q><L|R><cm>' = single leaf with clear width in cm and hand; 'JAMB' = a 50x100 jamb; anonymous '*U..' blocks = read the geometry. Use the decoded width to check rule 2's result, never as the primary signal.
proposedRules.covers: 6 of 6 _1D doors here (the width matches the jamb inner faces exactly).
proposedRules.failureCases: Useless for other offices and for anonymous dynamic blocks. Mirrored and rotated inserts change the hand.
proposedRules.howToCheck: Compare the decoded width with the measured clear width (0 mm difference on all 6 here).

proposedRules.rule: Heights and kinds. The plan has no heights (DSYM tags are empty; the 8 DW tags are on the elevation only). Doors: head at the project default (2.10 m) with a lintel up to the ceiling. Windows in a wall gap: default sill 0.90 m and head 2.10 m. Bays and glass screens: full height, flagged. Optionally read the elevation tags by aligning the elevation's grid labels with the plan.
proposedRules.covers: Lintels over all 32 doors and sills under 18 windows that sit in wall gaps; flags for 22 bays.
proposedRules.failureCases: Floor-length sliding doors drawn exactly like windows (most of the ground-floor glazing faces the terrace and pool). Elevation alignment is unproven.
proposedRules.howToCheck: Walk test in the viewer (all doors passable, no glass strips in doors). Staff review of flagged bays; spot-check against the 8 elevation tags.

surprises: Walls are drawn straight through 8 openings: doors G-D02, G-D09 and U-D05, and glass panels G-W09, G-W14, U-W02, U-W10 and U-W12. The merge closes all 8 with full-height wall solids. A gap-only detector cannot see them.
A closed room-outline polyline on WALL (handle E291, rectangle x 32.398-36.398, y 19.2585-23.109) crosses door G-D07, passage G-P06 and window G-W17. All three become 1 m 'single' colliders.

Door swings are on many layers: DOOR, layer 0 (9 unique arcs, including 2 pivot doors), WALL (inside hjkhkk), WIN (14 in the upper east block), and xref door layers with dashed linetypes (CENTER2, HIDDEN2).
WIN is used for doors as well as windows. 3-line WIN threshold bands across the upper north doors turn 3 door sets into glass strips, and 5 WIN door leaves become thin glass slabs.

Misleading layers: a washbasin block (A$C09C2022F) sits on WIN and becomes a glass solid. A sanitary-fitting chain is wrapped in INSERTs on DOOR and WALL. The OPEN layer is a 7.9 x 16.8 m zone outline. A wardrobe carcass is drawn on a wall layer.

Duplicates everywhere. Block hjkhkk (213 entities, holding most ground-floor windows and one door leaf) is inserted twice at the same point. The upper xref repeats its JAMB and D-JAMB pieces. A JAMB pair at x 26.65 is duplicated loose.
One LEAF insert (G-D08, plus its copies) has extrusion (0,0,-1). Its dxf.insert is in OCS, so prims.py stores x = -36.748 while the geometry is at +36.748.
Link-corridor and sliding-glass frames are drawn on the HATCH layer, with only one glass line on WIN or WALL-GL. These openings (G-W02, G-W06, G-W07, U-W07) are open holes in the merged model.
Two sliding units have D-JAMB pieces and slide arrows but no glass lines at all (G-W17, G-W20).

Leaf lengths are not opening widths. Loose LEAFs are 0.55 m in 0.60 m clear / 0.70 m structural openings. The *U31 frame in U-D02 sits 45-50 mm inside the wall gap. The _1D SWING arc is not centred on the hinge (about 23 mm off).

About half the glazed openings are whole bays between columns or perpendicular walls, with no collinear wall ends. No plan has a sill line, and the only door/window tags (D1, D3, AD1, AW1, AW12, AW14 x2, AW17) are on the right-hand elevation. Window vs floor-length glass cannot be decided from the plan.

Pocket sliding doors (3, upper floor) are drawn as 39 mm DOOR rectangles half inside wall slots. Two of them (U-D07, U-D08) have no wall gap, no arc and no jamb: the only openings no automatic signal found.

There are loose entities on top of the upper xref block (for example F960 and F961 at the top level inside the upper plan area), and a HIDDEN2 box on WALL marks an overhead element above passage U-P08.

Merged-model side effects: the front fence (W_Grill) and the pool glass (WALL-GL) became glass solids. The viewer extrudes glass from the floor to 0.6 m below the next level, so no window has a sill, and every glass solid blocks walking.
An orphan 1.08 m leaf rectangle on DOOR (handle C367) lies in the wall line at y 14.39-14.43, next to door G-D06 and the 2 m passage G-P07. It may be a sliding door; I left that open.
